A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same OpTI-BFM research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison; v2 retains the original material while expanding the appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original DMC control experiments, task-inference ablations, labeling-efficiency evaluations and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds navigation, optimization and robustness experiments in Appendices B.3–B.7.

M1.justification: The central regression, optimistic acquisition and Thompson-sampling procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 adds a gradient-ascent variant replacing random shooting, and B.4 adds behavior-cloning regularization to FB pretraining for navigation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates DMC locomotion and changing velocity targets. v2 extends coverage to five goal-navigation tasks in modified OGBench AntMaze, using near-expert navigation data, and adds nonlinear and noisy reward scenarios within Cheetah.

E2.justification: LoLA, Random, Oracle and RND retain their roles in the existing comparisons. v2 additionally evaluates OpTI-BFM+grad against the original optimizer in Figures 8, 9 and 18; this is an internal optimization variant, while the external baseline set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce substantial protocols: 1,000-step AntMaze episodes with widened goal rewards, gradient/sample-budget sweeps, 512 candidates sampled over the whole task space for successor-feature corruption, and controlled reward perturbations. These supplement the retained DMC protocol rather than establish revisions to its original experiments.

E4.justification: Appendices B.3 and B.5–B.7 add optimization-cost sensitivity, systematic successor-feature mismatch, nonlinear-reward projection-error and reward-noise analyses. Figure 10 also adds navigation trajectory examples. v1's update-frequency, warm-start and label-budget analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify min–max intervals across three training seeds, with means over 20 episodes for single-policy evaluation or 10 task-inference trials in Appendix E. No changed repetition policy, confidence-interval procedure or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: Original result plots and Table 1 values are retained. v2 adds navigation success rates, optimizer performance and speed comparisons, and results showing degradation under feature mismatch and slower convergence under noisy rewards, alongside nonlinear-reward comparisons in Figures 8–13 and 18.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.5 introduces bounded successor-feature and reward-misspecification assumptions, inflated confidence radii and a regret derivation with additional non-sublinear terms in Equations 71–105. The original ideal-assumption sublinear-regret analysis remains.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: optimistic online task inference, reduced reward-label requirements, regret guarantees for well-trained BFMs and adaptation within a few episodes. The appendix additions do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation of misspecification, optimization tradeoffs and failure conditions. It discusses irreducible uncertainty, favors random shooting for low-dimensional task spaces, and attributes additional nonlinear-reward sensitivity to using linearity for both collection and inference. B.6 explicitly qualifies its findings through changing reward scale and imperfect residual approximation.

D1.justification: The new experiments include implementation details such as Adam's 0.1 learning rate, optimizer-state retention and warm starts, a 0.01 behavior-cloning coefficient, and a normalized two-layer perturbation network. Existing architecture, training hyperparameters and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to misspecified bandits by Ghosh et al. and Bogunovic and Krause, OGBench, and Adam. These support localized appendix additions; the main related-work discussion and research positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main prose and section sequence are largely retained. Changes include local explanatory sentences, expanded appendix subsections, updated cross-references, author contact information and the conference-publication header.

P2.justification: Figures 8–13 and 18 add substantial visual material: optimizer comparisons, computational tradeoffs, navigation trajectories, projection-error scatterplots and robustness curves. Original figures are retained but relocated or renumbered; the two tables retain their contents and structure.

improvement.justification: The added optimization-cost and controlled robustness studies, together with modified AntMaze evaluation, improve empirical grounding and clarify failure conditions absent from v1. These gains are tempered by a gap in the new theoretical extension: Equation 95 substitutes true successor features into UCB although Equation 26 defines it using learned features, without justifying that substitution. Consequently, the added analysis does not securely resolve the theoretical approximation gap.
